insights.title: Brooks named the wedge himself - the AI-roadmap audit
insights.text: The single most valuable moment: Brooks, unprompted, described their confirmation/recency bias auditing their own AI build and asked whether ARCS could give an outside read on where they are on that arc and where hypotheses are failing. That is a founder handing you the sale's framing. The follow-up should lead with the audit, not the generic receipt/replay pitch Zach opened with.

insights.title: Their on-prem / SSOT anxieties are ARCS's native story
insights.text: Brooks wants an internal AI stack that's affordable, accurate, fast, cost-saving, and a single source of truth that isn't accreting data bloat and tech debt. ARCS's local-tenant / air-gap / composable-serializable design answers all of that directly. Emphasize the 'your PII stays local, I only add a meta-inference layer' framing - it lands hard with an on-prem-minded operator.

insights.title: Two on-ramps; keep the audit primary, the collab-risk model secondary
insights.text: A second, more tactical use case surfaced: early-signal risk screening for influencer collabs (the Riff Raff assault fallout; Neil Hamburger as a success). It's a real, vivid pain but narrower. Lead with the AI-roadmap audit (strategic, recurring, board-adjacent); hold the collab-risk model as a concrete demo taster, not the headline.

next_steps.text: FILE AN EX-ANTE FIRST (ADR-068 mandatory before any counterpart send), then send Brooks a tight materials packet framed around the AI-roadmap AUDIT he named: where are you on the arc / where's it inefficient / where are hypotheses failing - plus the composable conditional-workflow and persona-objection-handling angles. Register-fit: plain-language, non-fiction, Japanophile/omotenashi sensibility, zero vaporware.

Include one concrete demo hook: run the persona objection round-robin (how would Brooks / Justin / Jevin each eviscerate this, then the steelman) on one of THEIR real bets - a jerky flavor-drop go/no-go, or the internal-AI-build audit itself - as a taster of the engine, not a slide.

Hold the relationship map: Jevin ('Jeben') is the warm primary (many prior conversations, Stillwater/Wabi-Sabi lineage); Justin is secondary (one chat late July); Brooks is new but engaged. Justin + Jevin are the internal champions - keep them looped so the thread doesn't rest on a single new contact.

Set a follow-up cadence to beat the ghost risk: materials within days while warm, then a check-in at ~2 weeks. If silence reaches ~4 weeks with no scope conversation, mark the thread COOLED, not open - do not let a warm first call read as pipeline indefinitely.
